title: Tangent cone of a local polynomial ring at the closed origin
statement:
Let $(T,\mathfrak b)$ be a nonzero commutative Noetherian local ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], with residue field $\kappa=T/\mathfrak b$. Set $P=T[V]$, $\mathfrak q=\mathfrak bP+(V)$ and $U=P_{\mathfrak q}$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Then $\mathfrak q$ is maximal, $U$ is Noetherian local with maximal ideal $\mathfrak c=\mathfrak qU$ and residue field canonically $\kappa$, and there is a graded $\kappa$-algebra isomorphism
$$\Phi_T:(\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak b}T)[Z]\xrightarrow{\sim}\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak c}U,\qquad \deg Z=1,$$
where $\Phi_T$ sends the degree-$d$ class of $a\in\mathfrak b^d$ to the degree-$d$ class of $a/1$, and $Z$ to the degree-one class of $V/1$ [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. These isomorphisms commute with quotient maps: for any ideal $J\subseteq\mathfrak b$, the canonical map $U\to (T/J)[V]_{(\mathfrak b/J,V)}$ induces, under $\Phi_T$ and $\Phi_{T/J}$, the polynomial extension of $\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak b}T\to\operatorname{gr}_{\mathfrak b/J}(T/J)$. If $T$ is regular local [def-weil-regular-scheme], then $U$ is regular local.

source.place: Hironaka, Certain numerical characters of singularities (1970), Remark (10.1), p.165, Proposition 11, p.166, and proof of Lemma 12, pp.166--167: local polynomial associated graded isomorphism, its coefficient inclusion and extension of the initial ideal. Naturality for quotient maps is the coefficient form of those identifications. Read online at https://scispace.com/pdf/certain-numerical-characters-of-singularities-18d51ii5bz.pdf; archival copy WANTED. No Stacks tag states this entire natural comparison.

proof.text: Evaluation at $V=0$ followed by $T\to\kappa$ is surjective with kernel $\mathfrak q$: a polynomial is in the kernel exactly when its constant coefficient belongs to $\mathfrak b$, since its remaining terms are divisible by $V$ [def-weil-polynomial-ring]. Thus $P/\mathfrak q=\kappa$ and $\mathfrak q$ is maximal. The localization definition [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] gives a local ring $U$ with maximal ideal $\mathfrak c=\mathfrak qU$. Its residue map is explicitly $f/s\mapsto\overline{f(0)}/\overline{s(0)}$. The denominator is nonzero because $s\notin\mathfrak q$; the kernel consists exactly of fractions with numerator in $\mathfrak q$, so this gives $U/\mathfrak c\simeq\kappa$.

source.place: Elementary ideal-power and fraction calculations from the definitions of polynomial rings and localization (Tags 00CO, 07BH); detailed agent proof of the comparison asserted in Hironaka, Proposition 11, p.166, and used in Lemma 12, pp.166--167.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] to $T\to P=T[V]$ (one generator and zero relation ideal), and then [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian] to $P\to U$ at $P\setminus\mathfrak q$. Hence $P$ and $U$ are Noetherian. These uses require only the given Noetherianity of $T$, not its regularity.

Expand the power of the sum of ideals by distributivity: for $n\geq0$,
$$\mathfrak q^n=\sum_{j=0}^n\mathfrak b^{n-j}V^jP.$$
For completeness the base $n=0$ is $P=P$; multiplying the displayed sum by $\mathfrak bP+(V)$ gives the same sum with $n$ replaced by $n+1$, including its two endpoints. Consequently $f=\sum_i a_iV^i$ lies in $\mathfrak q^n$ exactly when $a_i\in\mathfrak b^{n-i}$ for $0\leq i<n$, with no restriction for $i\geq n$: each summand on the right has this property, and conversely each term with $i<n$ belongs to its $j=i$ summand while every term with $i\geq n$ belongs to $V^nP$. This uses only polynomial coefficients [def-weil-polynomial-ring] and ideal multiplication.

proof.text:
Using the preceding coefficient criterion for $n$ and $n+1$, coefficient extraction and its inverse give
$$\bigoplus_{i=0}^n\mathfrak b^{n-i}/\mathfrak b^{n-i+1}\ \xrightarrow{\sim}\ \mathfrak q^n/\mathfrak q^{n+1},\qquad ([a_i])_{i=0}^n\longmapsto[\sum_{i=0}^n a_iV^i].$$
Indeed every term of exponent greater than $n$ is zero in this quotient, and the displayed sum is zero exactly when each $a_i\in\mathfrak b^{n-i+1}$. In particular the formula is independent of lifts. These are $\kappa$-linear maps, because $\mathfrak b$ kills each source summand and $\mathfrak q$ kills the target [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring].

proof.text:
For every $N\geq1$ and $s\notin\mathfrak q$, write $s=s_0+Vh$ with $s_0\in T\setminus\mathfrak b$. Since $T$ is local, $s_0$ is a unit. Put $w=s_0^{-1}Vh\in\mathfrak q$. In $P/\mathfrak q^N$ the inverse of $s$ is
$$s_0^{-1}\sum_{j=0}^{N-1}(-w)^j,$$
as multiplication gives $1-(-w)^N=1$. Thus the fraction rule gives an inverse $U/\mathfrak c^N\to P/\mathfrak q^N$, $[f/s]\mapsto[f][s]^{-1}$, to $[f]\mapsto[f/1]$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. It is well defined by the fraction equality relation, and $\mathfrak c^N=\mathfrak q^NU$ because extending ideals commutes with finite sums of products. It sends $\mathfrak c^n/\mathfrak c^{n+1}$ onto $\mathfrak q^n/\mathfrak q^{n+1}$ for $N=n+1$: a numerator from $\mathfrak q^n$ stays there when multiplied by the displayed polynomial inverse. Hence localization induces a bijection on these pieces for every $n\geq0$, including $n=0$.

proof.text:
Compose the degreewise maps of steps 4 and 5. On a homogeneous polynomial term $[a]_d Z^i$, the resulting map is $[aV^i/1]_{d+i}$. It is bijective in degree $n$ by those steps. It preserves products since
$$([a]_dZ^i)([b]_eZ^j)=[ab]_{d+e}Z^{i+j},\qquad (aV^i/1)(bV^j/1)=abV^{i+j}/1.$$
It preserves addition, $1$, and the degree-zero copy of $\kappa$ by the same formulas. Finite sums of homogeneous terms exhaust both rings, by the definitions of polynomial and associated graded rings [def-weil-polynomial-ring, def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. This gives the required graded $\kappa$-algebra isomorphism $\Phi_T$, with precisely its stated coefficient and variable images.

proof.text:
Let $J\subseteq\mathfrak b$. Ideals of $T/J$ lift to ideals of $T$ containing $J$, so their finite generators project to finite generators; $T/J$ is Noetherian. Its units are exactly the classes outside $\mathfrak b/J$, so it is nonzero local with this maximal ideal and residue field $\kappa$. A denominator $s\notin\mathfrak q$ remains outside $(\mathfrak b/J,V)$ because its constant coefficient has nonzero image in $\kappa$. Therefore $f/s\mapsto\bar f/\bar s$ defines the canonical localization map [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. It sends $\mathfrak c^n$ into the corresponding $n$th power, and so induces the associated graded map [def-weil-pbc-associated-graded-ring]. On every homogeneous term the two maps in the claimed square are both
$$[a]_dZ^i\longmapsto[\bar aV^i/1]_{d+i}.$$
Here the coefficient map is $[a]_d\mapsto[a+J]_d$ in $((\mathfrak b/J)^d/(\mathfrak b/J)^{d+1})$, which is well defined since powers map to powers. Equality on finite sums proves the required quotient compatibility.

proof.text: Finally suppose $T$ is regular local. By the last sentence of [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-localization], $T$ is a regular ring. Apply [lem-trf-polynomial-ring-regular-base] with one variable: $P$ is regular. By the definition of regular ring [def-weil-regular-scheme], its localization at the prime $\mathfrak q$ is regular local. This is $U$ from step 1, proving the last clause without assuming that the possibly singular ring $T/J$ is regular.
